name: Shape language
controls: The family of forms every element is built from: corners, curves, angles, regularity and repetition across shapes, containers, icons and illustration.
question: What kind of shapes should everything be built from?
notes: Shape language is the strongest personality lever after color. Corner radius: 0px reads engineered, brutal or editorial; 4-8px reads professional UI; 16-32px reads friendly consumer product; fully round (pill, circle) reads playful and soft. Continuous-curvature corners (squircles, as in Apple's app icon mask) read more premium than plain circular-arc radii at the same size. Stroke thickness scales perceived weight: hairlines feel precise and fragile, heavy strokes feel bold and childlike. Repetition of one shape creates system and brand recognition; mixing many unrelated shapes reads chaotic unless deliberate (Memphis). Symmetry reads stable, formal and trustworthy; asymmetry reads dynamic and human. Irregularity (hand-drawn wobble, organic edges) reads human, warm and imperfect; perfect regularity reads machine-made. Motion follows shape: sharp shapes suit fast linear or snappy eases and rigid rotation; round and soft shapes suit springy eases and squash; organic shapes suit morphing. Many terms here overlap (soft, rounded, inflated); pick the one that names the dominant trait, and at most two.

options.what: Forms built from straight lines and right angles, with square corners.
options.looks: Rectangles, squares, orthogonal lines, 0px radius, crisp alignment.
options.motion: Rigid slides along axes, wipes, snapping; linear or expo eases, no squash.
options.use: Editorial, architectural, brutalist and Swiss-influenced brands, fintech, dev tools.
options.vs: Grid-based concerns placement on a grid; rectilinear concerns the forms themselves. Sharp includes acute angles; rectilinear is only 90 degrees.
options.prompt: Build every shape, card, button and container with 0px corner radius and only horizontal and vertical edges; align everything to a grid. Move elements only along x or y axes with expo.inOut or power4.out, no rotation, no squash.

options.what: Rectangles and forms with moderately rounded corners.
options.looks: Cards and buttons with 12-24px radii (at 1080p), soft edges but still rectangular structure.
options.motion: Smooth scale and slide transitions, gentle overshoot, Flip layout changes.
options.use: Modern SaaS, consumer apps, most contemporary product UI.
options.vs: Pill is fully rounded ends; soft adds low-contrast softness beyond corners; rectilinear has 0px.
options.prompt: Use a consistent corner radius system: 24px on large cards, 16px on medium containers, 12px on buttons and inputs (1080p); nested radii equal outer radius minus padding. Animate with power3.out and at most back.out(1.2) overshoot.

options.what: Elongated shapes with fully semicircular ends (radius equal to half the height).
options.looks: Pill buttons, tags, toggles, capsule containers, rounded bars.
options.motion: Stretching and contracting along length, morphing between pill and circle, liquid-feeling transitions.
options.use: Consumer apps, tags and chips, dynamic-island-style UI, playful brands.
options.vs: Rounded shapes have radius less than half the height; circular shapes are pills with equal width and height.
options.prompt: Make buttons, tags and containers pill-shaped (border-radius 9999px). Transition between states by stretching width with the height fixed (500ms ease power3.inOut) and morphing pill to circle and back; content cross-fades in the middle of the stretch.

options.what: Forms based on circles, rings and arcs.
options.looks: Dots, circles, rings, arcs, concentric shapes, radial arrangements.
options.motion: Rotation, radial expansion, ripples, orbiting, arc draw-ons.
options.use: Loading and progress, audio, wellness, ecosystem diagrams, dotted brand systems.
options.vs: Geometric includes circles plus squares and triangles; blob shapes are irregular round forms.
options.prompt: Build the visual system from circles, rings (2-4px strokes) and arcs only; containers become circles or pills. Animate with scale from center, ring ripples (scale 1 to 2.5, opacity 1 to 0, 1.2s ease power2.out) and rotating arcs.

options.what: Pure primitive shapes (circle, square, triangle, semicircle) combined systematically.
options.looks: Flat primitives, Bauhaus-like compositions, strong color blocks, precise construction.
options.motion: Primitives assembling and disassembling, rotating in 90-degree steps, shape-to-shape morphs.
options.use: Brand identities, abstract explainers, education, design-led tech.
options.vs: Rectilinear is only straight lines; circular is only curves; geometric combines primitives. Technical adds detail and annotation.
options.prompt: Build compositions only from circles, squares, triangles and semicircles in 3-4 flat colors, on a grid. Animate by assembling primitives (scale 0 to 1 from their own centers, stagger 60ms), rotating in 90-degree steps, and morphing one primitive into another.

options.what: Forms dominated by diagonals, chamfered corners and non-right angles.
options.looks: Slanted edges, chamfered or clipped corners, parallelograms, chevrons, dynamic diagonals.
options.motion: Diagonal wipes, slashing transitions, fast directional motion.
options.use: Gaming, sports, esports, automotive, action-oriented brands.
options.vs: Sharp is about pointed acute corners; angular is about diagonal edges and chamfers, not necessarily pointed. Rectilinear is right angles only.
options.prompt: Cut shapes with diagonals: chamfer container corners 16-24px (clip-path polygon), skew bars -12 degrees, use parallelogram banners and chevrons. Move elements along diagonals with fast power4.out eases (250-400ms) and slash wipes at 20-30 degrees.

options.what: Forms with pointed, acute corners and crisp tips.
options.looks: Spikes, stars, triangles, pointed shards, knife-edge corners.
options.motion: Stabbing and snapping motion, shattering, quick rotations.
options.use: Music and culture, gaming, security, edgy fashion and streetwear.
options.vs: Angular uses diagonals and chamfers that can be blunt; sharp emphasizes acute points. Rectilinear has 90-degree corners.
options.prompt: Use acute-angled forms: triangles, shards and stars with tips under 45 degrees, 0px radius everywhere. Animate with snaps (100-200ms, power4.out), shatter transitions (shape splits into 8-12 shards that fly out) and no easing softness.

options.what: Natural, flowing forms derived from living things: leaves, pebbles, water.
options.looks: Asymmetric curves, varying thickness, natural silhouettes, no straight lines.
options.motion: Growth, swaying, flowing, breathing, gentle morphing.
options.vs: Blob shapes are simple amorphous masses; organic shapes reference nature more specifically. Irregular is unpredictability without natural reference.
options.prompt: Draw shapes with only curves (no straight edges or equal radii), inspired by pebbles, leaves and water; vary contour thickness. Animate with slow growth (scale from base, 1.2-2s ease sine.out), swaying (rotation +-3 degrees, 3s sine.inOut), and gentle path morphs.

options.what: Soft, amorphous, rounded masses without defined corners or structure.
options.looks: Wobbly rounded forms, liquid silhouettes, gradient blobs in the background.
options.motion: Continuous morphing, wobbling, merging and splitting (metaball).
options.use: Background ambience, AI and wellness brands, playful consumer apps.
options.vs: Organic references nature; blobs are abstract. Inflated shapes are pressurized volumes with highlights.
options.prompt: Use 1-4 blob shapes (8-12 point closed bezier paths) as main forms or background; morph each between 3 variants on a continuous 4-6s loop (MorphSVGPlugin, ease sine.inOut). For merging, apply a gooey filter (blur 10 plus alpha threshold).

options.what: Deliberately inconsistent forms: uneven sizes, wonky edges and unpredictable proportions.
options.looks: No two shapes alike, uneven edges, off-kilter angles, cut-paper feel.
options.motion: Stepped or jittery motion, uneven timing, randomized stagger.
options.use: Culture and art brands, anti-corporate campaigns, zines, youth content.
options.vs: Hand-drawn shows the pen stroke; irregular is about the form itself. Organic is flowing and natural; irregular can be jagged.
options.prompt: Make every shape slightly different: vary sizes +-20%, rotate +-8 degrees, give edges small random deviations (3-6px), no identical repeats. Animate with random stagger ({ each: 0.05, from: 'random' }) and slightly uneven durations (+-15%).

options.what: Shapes that visibly come from a drawing hand: wobbly contours, overshoots and pressure variation.
options.looks: Wobbly outlines, fills that miss the lines, sketchy hatching, marker texture.
options.use: Education, whiteboard explainers, creative tools, community brands.
options.vs: Irregular is about proportion; hand-drawn is about line quality. See the stroke dimension for line treatment.
options.prompt: Draw every shape with wobbly contours (2-4px deviation), slight overshoots at corners and fills offset 3-5px from their outlines. Draw shapes on with stroke-dashoffset, then boil: cycle 3 redrawn versions every 3 frames.

options.what: Shapes built from repeated identical units that combine into larger forms.
options.looks: Tiles, blocks, segments, pixels or bricks assembling into letters, icons and scenes.
options.motion: Units assembling and disassembling, cascading tile flips, rearrangement.
options.use: Brand systems, data products, gaming, platform and building-block metaphors.
options.vs: Grid-based places elements on a grid; modular builds forms out of repeated units.
options.prompt: Construct every larger form from one repeated unit (e.g. a 40px rounded square or a quarter-circle tile) in 2-3 colors. Assemble forms by animating units into place (stagger 20ms from center, 400ms ease power3.out) and rearrange units to form the next shape.

options.what: Shapes sized and positioned strictly according to an underlying grid.
options.looks: Consistent spacing, aligned edges, shapes in grid multiples, sometimes a visible grid.
options.motion: Snapping between grid positions, row/column staggers, grid-cell reveals.
options.use: Swiss-influenced brands, dashboards, data and infrastructure products.
options.vs: Modular builds forms from units; grid-based governs placement and proportion. Composition dimension covers grid layouts as systems.
options.prompt: Size every shape in multiples of an 8px base unit and 40px grid cells; align all edges to the grid (optionally show it as 1px lines at 8% opacity). Move shapes by whole cells with power3.inOut, staggering by row or column.

options.what: Low-contrast, gentle forms with generous rounding, blurred edges or feathered transitions.
options.looks: Generous radii (24px+), soft gradients, feathered or blurred shapes, pastel or muted color.
options.motion: Slow, eased, floaty motion; cross-fades and gentle scales; nothing snaps.
options.use: Wellness, meditation, AI assistants, healthcare, premium lifestyle.
options.vs: Rounded is only about corners; soft is the whole shape impression, including edge blur and contrast. Inflated is soft plus volume.
options.prompt: Use generously rounded shapes (radius 32px+ or fully organic), low-contrast fills, edges softened with 0-4px blur or gradient falloff, no hard outlines. Animate slowly (800-1400ms) with ease sine.inOut or power2.out; no snaps or overshoots.

options.what: Shapes that look pressurized and volumetric, like balloons or cushions.
options.looks: Swollen rounded forms, glossy or soft highlights, inner shading, seams pulled in.
options.motion: Inflating from flat, jiggling on impact, squash and stretch, deflating.
options.use: Playful consumer brands, 3D social content, kids, Y2K revival.
options.vs: Soft is flat and calm; inflated is volumetric and bouncy. Blob is amorphous; inflated usually keeps a recognizable form (an icon or letter) swollen.
options.prompt: Render shapes as inflated volumes: radial highlight top-left, inner shadow along the lower edge, soft contact shadow, fully rounded silhouette. Enter by inflating: scale 0.2 to 1.1 to 0.97 to 1 over 700ms (ease elastic.out(1, 0.45)) with a 60ms scaleY lag.

options.what: Precise engineered forms with construction details: crosshairs, brackets, tick marks, cutaways.
options.looks: Thin precise lines, corner brackets, measurement marks, grid overlays, monospace labels.
options.motion: Measured, precise draw-ons, scanning lines, readouts updating.
options.use: Developer tools, hardware, security, AI infrastructure, aerospace.
options.vs: Geometric is simple primitives; technical adds schematic annotation. Rectilinear is only straight lines.
options.prompt: Frame elements with technical details: 1-1.5px lines, 12px corner brackets, crosshairs at key points, tick marks every 8px on edges, small monospace labels. Draw details on precisely (stroke-dashoffset 300-500ms, ease power1.inOut) and add a scanning line pass.
